tagline: Across southern New Hartford, where the Nepaug meets its reservoir.
intro: US 202 crosses the southern part of New Hartford for about five miles to the Canton line, in a mostly rural town of farms, homes and parks. The road was Route 4, and later Route 25, before US 202 took it over in 1974.

The road's main event is water. The Nepaug River runs down to the US 202 bridge and there enters the Nepaug Reservoir, about two miles long and a mile wide, made by the Nepaug Dam and managed by the Metropolitan District Commission.

moments.title: Gillette's Grist Mill
moments.text: Off Maple Hollow Road on the Nepaug stands a rare grist mill that still has its water wheel and iron gears of about 1870, though it stopped grinding by 1880.

moments.title: Nepaug River bridge
moments.text: Paddlers run Class I and II water down the Nepaug as far as this bridge, where the river slides into the northwest corner of the reservoir.
